Title: Boulder City Council Regular Meeting - August 3, 2023

Topic1.Title: Call to Order, Agenda Amendment, and Roll Call
Topic1.Summary: Council called the meeting to order and unanimously amended the agenda to add a birthday song for Councilmember Tara Leonard. Roll call was then taken with all members present, though Tim Wallach attended virtually. The agenda was confirmed as amended before moving to the next items.

Topic2.Title: Pollinator and Little Creature Appreciation Declaration
Topic2.Summary: Councilmember Yates presented a declaration recognizing August and September 2023 as a time to celebrate pollinators and other little creatures, with children from the community participating. Staff and speakers highlighted upcoming free events, including an exhibit at the library gallery and the Boulder Pollinator Festival on September 9th in Central Park. The declaration emphasizes the importance of insects to ecosystems, food supply, and human well-being, and commits the city to community action.

Topic3.Title: Public Participation
Topic3.Summary: Staff reviewed the city's public participation guidelines, which prohibit threats, intimidation, and disruptive behavior and limit remarks to city business. Community members spoke on topics including a proposed homeless daycare center on Folsom Street, bird habitat preservation, camping for people experiencing homelessness, mental health and criminal justice concerns, historic preservation of the Boulder Bandshell area, minimum wage increases, bus service frequency, BHP lease paperwork, and occupancy limits. Staff and council members acknowledged the concerns and noted follow-up actions, including referrals to other agencies and an email response on the BHP leases.

Topic4.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic4.Summary: Council considered a consent agenda of items 3A through 3E, including the first reading of an occupancy ordinance (3B). Councilmember Weiner, Yates, and Mayor Pro Tem Wallach voted against item 3B, while the remaining items passed unanimously. Councilmember Wallach and staff noted that a public hearing on occupancy would be held at second reading on August 17th.

Topic5.Title: Call-Up Check-Ins
Topic5.Summary: Council reviewed three call-up items: an extension of the call-up period for a landmark alteration certificate to remove a fence in Chautauqua Park, a site review amendment to expand the Orchard PUD property at 1576 Hawthorne Avenue, and a use review for a restaurant patio expansion at 4910 and 4920 Knox Court North. No council members called up any of the items. The call-up period concluded without further action.

Topic6.Title: Public Hearing: Powers House Individual Landmark Designation (Ordinance 8580)
Topic6.Summary: Staff presented the proposal to designate 830 14th Street as the Powers House, an individual landmark, noting it is a 1920 Craftsman Bungalow within the University Place historic district. The property owners declined to speak, and one public commenter criticized the landmarks board process. Council unanimously adopted Ordinance 8580 designating the property as an individual landmark.

Topic7.Title: Public Hearing: 2023 Ballot Measures
Topic7.Summary: Council reviewed five ballot-related ordinances, including a safe zones for kids petition, Charter amendments on election procedures, and three measures on extending the 0.15 percent sales and use tax. The Arts for Boulder petition sought 100 percent of the tax for arts and culture, staff proposed 100 percent for the general fund, and a compromise measure proposed a 50/50 split. After public comment and extensive discussion, Council passed Ordinance 8591 (the 50/50 compromise) as amended by a 7-2 vote, and Ordinance 8589 (the arts petition) as amended, with the other ordinances deferred to August 17th.

Topic8.Title: Matters from the City Manager: 311 Mapleton Land Dedication Update
Topic8.Summary: Staff updated Council on the 311 Mapleton development, where the developer originally committed to eight on-site affordable units and a senior affordable housing site at Fruhof. The developer later paid cash in lieu, and the original agreement expired, reverting the requirement to 20 percent inclusionary housing. Staff negotiated a new agreement under which the developer will donate the Fruhof site to the city, which will transfer it to Boulder Housing Partners, and pay $1.7 million in cash in lieu, totaling about $8 million in value versus $3.8 million legally required. Closing is expected soon, and Council praised staff's work and emphasized the need to improve processes for future agreements.

Topic9.Title: Homeless Services External Evaluation and Safe Outdoor Camping Update
Topic9.Summary: Staff described plans for an external evaluation of the homeless services system, to be conducted jointly with Boulder County and Longmont, with an RFP expected in September and work beginning in January 2024. Staff reported on research into safe outdoor camping programs in other cities and city-owned sites, and Council discussed urgency, cold-weather planning, and whether to add safe outdoor spaces to the work plan. Council directed staff to modify the RFP to include an examination of safe outdoor spaces and micro communities, and to evaluate Boulder's unique homelessness needs and gaps. Staff agreed to return sooner with a timeline and resource assessment for adding safe outdoor spaces to the work plan.
